reason: The hypothesis combines the superior oxidation resistance of HfB2 (P6) with the scale-stabilizing effect of Y-doping observed in HEA coatings (P7, P31) and transfers this combined idea to a new environment (molten aluminum corrosion) and a new material system (Y2O3-doped HfB2 coating), proposing a specific mechanism (Y-stabilized HfO2 scale) that none of the passages states for this application. This represents a synthesis of findings from different papers into a new proposal.
copied_elements: HfB2 as a baseline boride with good oxidation resistance (P6)
Y and Hf co-doping improves high-temperature oxidation resistance and reduces scale spallation (P7, P31)
formation of a dense HfO2 protective layer (P7, P9, P12)
use of laser cladding for coating deposition (P31)
